title: The Movement
canon: New York City, September through November 2012, across the collegiate fall term and the mayoral election. Seven gifted international students at a Columbia-like university in upper Manhattan are secretly recruited into the Lab for International Specialists and trained through covert missions by the Professor, who serves the Unknown Global Consortium. While the seven believe they are defending Mayor Grace Camarda's re-election against UGC-backed billionaire Ben Gilman, every mission secretly bends the race the consortium's way. EP101 'CHAMBERS' (draft v02) opens the recruitment as a public fellowship hackathon with eight finalists and seven seats: Devon Okafor-Reyes, the best of them, is cut for being unusable — his instinct is to erase records, and the UGC keeps them — and the machine quietly dismantles his life while the seven celebrate on a rooftop.
look: Marco's canon names the look outright: the Bourne series — kinetic handheld camera, staccato energy, stark contrast, realism. 2012 New York in the fall, shot as if by a documentary crew embedded with the students: available light only, cold institutional daylight, sodium and fluorescent city night, green banker's lamps in the library. Nothing stylized or futuristic; the conspiracy hides inside an ordinary, believable city. Every frame full-bleed, no letterbox.
note: Light Law pass 2026-07-18 — prompts from movement-canon.md + ep101-chambers-v02.md. Eight new moment-in-time frames (Marco's 2026-07-18 standard: human emotion is the story — a touch, an embrace, a tear, a look held too long). All eight derive from EP101 'CHAMBERS' v02, the page where canon is thinner; canon supplies period, geography, and the Columbia-like campus ('September 2012: New York City', 'a university not unlike Columbia University in Manhattan'). SEVEN-FACES CANON RULING STILL OPEN (carried forward from the old spec): 01-seven-students-fog.png remains the only de facto cast for the seven and is used as ref wherever one of the seven appears with a visible face — Marco should rule before wide generation. Devon, Rosa, and the Janitor are not among the seven and have no refs; their prompts own the descriptions from the page. Period held at fall 2012 per canon; the draft's tap-to-pay beat is rendered period-correct as a MetroCard swipe, and the draft's period flag ('Contemporary' vs 2012) still awaits Marco's reconciliation. No shot duplicates the twelve in specs/11-08-movement.json. RULINGS 2026-09-02 (Marco): period is 2012 (MetroCard, not tap-to-pay). Keep the seven faces from 01-seven-students-fog.png as the de facto cast for now — 'doesn't matter for now'; no wide-generation block on this.

stills.prompt: The turnstile bank of the 116th Street IRT station under Broadway, Morningside Heights, Manhattan, a September morning in 2012. An eighteen-year-old kid, backpack worn on both shoulders, leans across and swipes his own yellow MetroCard through the reader for a stranger — a sun-browned young man in his early twenties with a canvas field bag and a hole at the toe of one sneaker, caught mid-embarrassment, his own bent card useless in his fist. Their eyes meet over the turnstile arm; the kid is already half turned into his own morning. The only light: the station's flat greenish fluorescents doubled in the white wall tile, one shaft of grey daylight down the street stairs. Handheld eye-level frame, 35mm film still, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: A four-story glass atrium on a Columbia-like campus in Morningside Heights, Manhattan, September 2012, a live selection ceremony. On the screen wall behind the stage, eight student portraits — seven blooming warm gold, one still dark. Beneath his own dark portrait an eighteen-year-old finalist claps for the winners, grin held half a second past its life, eyes wet and furious and still smiling, the badge on his chest unlit. Around him the seven chosen embrace, soft, out of focus; families on their feet. Light only as found: the gold bloom of the lit portraits on faces, the cold spill of the screen wall, mixed temperatures, half his face falling into shadow. Handheld long lens from inside the crowd, 35mm film still, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: A bare concrete fire stairwell behind a glass atrium building in Morningside Heights, Manhattan, night, September 2012. A Japanese student of twenty-three sits alone on a step in party clothes, no phone anywhere. Her forearm is turned up and she rubs her thumb hard across a short line of handwritten ballpoint ink, smudged past reading — it smears and does not vanish — and she stares at it the way people stare at something they are about to betray. Light only as found: one caged fluorescent tube on the landing throwing hard flat light down the steps, and the green wash of an exit sign over the door below, its face out of frame. Handheld from a half flight above, 35mm film still, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: The rooftop of a campus building above Morningside Heights, Manhattan, night, September 2012, a private party for seven students. At the parapet rail, apart from the others, a dark-haired Basque woman of twenty-two touches her champagne flute against a young American man's — not a toast, glass barely meeting glass — and they look at each other instead of the city. Behind them the other five laugh under strings of party bulbs and propane heat lamps; far below, two rival campaign billboards face each other, lettering soft and unreadable. Light only as found: the warm string bulbs, heat-lamp glow on one side of each face, the cold shimmer of a million lit windows beyond, deep shadow between them. stills.prompt: The stoop of a brick rowhouse in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, night, autumn 2012. In the half-open doorway a grandmother in her seventies — apron still on — slowly lowers a cordless phone from her chest, the call still open, and looks down at her grandson: an eighteen-year-old on the steps below, looking back up at her, having just told her the truth. Something has gone out of her face; she is not crying, and that is worse. Light only as found: the gold kitchen light behind her cutting her outline and spilling thin down the steps, the sodium streetlamp laying orange across the sidewalk, the faint blue of his phone face-up on the step. Handheld from the sidewalk, low, 35mm film still, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.
